title: A living sacrifice (Romans 12)
hook: rejoice with them that rejoice, weep with them that weep

segments.voice: Yesterday, the great list in Romans 8. Your line was nothing shall separate us.

Your phone buzzes twice in the same hour. One friend: we're engaged! Another: my dad's in the hospital. Two messages, two completely different rooms to walk into, and both need you. For eleven chapters, Romans has been about grace, faith and God's love. In chapter twelve, Paul turns to what all that looks like on an ordinary day. A lot of it sounds like an answer to those two messages.
screen: `TWO MESSAGES IN ONE HOUR.` → `ELEVEN CHAPTERS OF GRACE.` → `THEN: WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE.`

segments.voice: It opens with a strange phrase, in the Douay-Rheims: "I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercy of God, that you present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, pleasing unto God, your reasonable service." In Paul's world, a sacrifice was offered at an altar, and it usually died. Paul flips it: offer yourselves, but alive. Your bodies, meaning your whole selves: your hands, your time, your Tuesday. Reasonable service, logike latreia, can mean worship that fits who you are, the worship of mind and heart. Then: don't be conformed to this world, but be made new in your mind. And Paul gets very practical. You're one body with many members and different gifts. Let love be without pretending. Outdo one another in showing honor. Be patient in tribulation, steady in prayer. Share with the saints in need. And: "Rejoice with them that rejoice; weep with them that weep." Both halves are hard. Weeping with someone means staying in the hospital room instead of fixing things. Rejoicing can be harder: being glad at a friend's engagement, with no envy in it, when your own life seems stalled. Paul puts them side by side as one living sacrifice. The chapter ends: don't be overcome by evil, but overcome evil by good. A living sacrifice isn't a dramatic moment. It's showing up, again and again, in whichever room you're needed.
screen: `A SACRIFICE THAT STAYS ALIVE.` · `LOGIKE LATREIA: FITTING WORSHIP.` · `ONE BODY, MANY GIFTS.` · `REJOICE WITH THEM, WEEP WITH THEM.` · then, large: `OVERCOME EVIL BY GOOD.`

segments.voice: Think of two people: one with good news right now, and one who is hurting. Picture the first and give gladness for them some room, no comparing, setting envy down kindly if it shows up; then stay a moment with the second and what they're carrying, without rushing to fix it. If you pray, offer your body, your time and hands, as Paul says.
Reasonable service. Paul's phrase for offering your whole self, alive, as worship: logike latreia, the worship of mind and heart. Today's word.
Your line: rejoice and weep with them. Both rooms need you. That's day five hundred sixty-eight.

screen: `DAY 568 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE FOOLISHNESS OF THE CROSS.`

howItsDone: At Mass, the priest invites the people to pray that the sacrifice, his and theirs, be acceptable to God, and Catholics speak of offering their whole day, work, joys and sufferings, as a living sacrifice, often through a morning offering.

fork.setup: in the same hour, one friend announces an engagement and another's father is rushed to hospital. Paul's advice?
options: focus only on the one in trouble.
rejoice with one and weep with the other.
fork.reveal: rejoice with them that rejoice; weep with them that weep. both are part of the living sacrifice.

original.note: Greek: reasonable, fitting worship, the worship of mind and heart. Paul's name for offering yourself alive.

trapdoor: what you thought: sacrifice means giving something up.
what it means: Paul asks for a sacrifice that stays alive: your whole self, offered in daily love, joy and grief shared.
what a scholar hears: logikē latreia has been translated reasonable service, spiritual worship, and worship of the mind. latreia was the word for temple service.
recall: power, Paul's word for the gospel

chat.says: What does Paul mean by being a living sacrifice?
options: Offering your whole self, hands and time, alive, as worship that shows up for others.
Putting money in the collection, since that's the offering Paul means here.
Setting aside one day a week for church, as a gift of your time to God.
chat.meaning: In Romans 12, the sacrifice stays alive: your whole self offered as worship, rejoicing and weeping with others.

logike latreia.meaning: Greek: reasonable, fitting worship, of mind and heart

brethren.meaning: an old word for brothers, fellow believers
